analysis.title: October CPI: no reprieve from high inflation
key_insights: Core CPI rose 0.3% m/m in October and headline CPI rose 0.4% m/m. Core came in above expectations for the third straight month.
Core inflation strength was broad-based, with above-trend increases in core services and core goods. Shelter was the biggest contributor, followed by transportation and recreation services.

Core goods inflation slowed to 0.16% m/m from 0.25% in September, almost entirely because of a drop in used car prices. Outside of autos, core goods inflation accelerated at its fastest pace all year.

Core services ex-shelter (supercore) rose 0.39% m/m in October and has been firm for four months. It has risen at a 4.7% annualized pace over the past three months. PNC says the Fed needs it closer to 0.2% m/m to return core inflation to target.

PNC reads elevated supercore inflation as a sign that demand is outstripping supply, and says the Fed's inflation problem is fundamentally a demand problem. It says the trend is difficult to explain away with energy prices or tariffs.

The supercore increase was driven largely by transportation prices, including a stronger rise in insurance pricing. Insurance is not relevant for PCE inflation, so PPI data is more relevant for the PCE read.
Shelter added about 0.14 percentage points to the 0.30% core increase, slightly below its contribution in September. Shelter rose 0.30% m/m versus 0.39% in September.
Core CPI has risen at a 3.7% annualized pace over the past three months.
The year-over-year CPI figure was not released because there was no October 2025 CPI release, which was disrupted by the government shutdown.

Markets priced December rate hike odds at just over 100% after the print, which includes some chance of a 50bps hike on top of a fully priced 25bps hike. PNC expects a 25bps hike in December and sees a 50bps hike as less likely.
PNC says it would expect the Fed to consider a 50bps move if later data show a sharper reacceleration or if inflation expectations deteriorate. Friday's PPI will help estimate October core PCE.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Hotter than expected, third straight monthly beat, though slightly below September's 0.65%.
Above expectations for the third straight month, with little sign of moderation. September was 0.33%.
Core inflation continues at a pace well above target.
Accelerated from 0.34% in September, driven by transportation and insurance. PNC says it needs to fall closer to 0.2%.
PNC says this is far from the pace the Fed needs to return inflation to target.
Down from 0.25% in September on used car prices. Ex-autos, it was the fastest pace of the year.
Down from 0.39% in September but still the largest contributor to core CPI.
Market pricing after the print: a fully priced 25bps hike plus some chance of 50bps.
PNC's view that the print strengthens the case for a quarter-point hike. A 50bps hike remains less likely in its view.

risk_factors: Higher energy and commodity prices could leak into core goods prices, taking over from the tariff effect, which appears to have waned after peaking earlier this year.
Supercore inflation staying well above levels consistent with the Fed's 2% target.
A sharper reacceleration in inflation or worsening inflation expectations could move the Fed toward a 50bps hike.
Fed Governor Waller said before the CPI release that the Fed could consider a 50bps move in December.

tension_points.bull_case: Waller said before the CPI release that the Fed could consider a 50bps move in December. Markets priced some chance of 50bps on top of a full 25bps hike after the print.
tension_points.bear_case: PNC says a 50bps hike is still unlikely because CPI inflation did not accelerate from the prior release. It expects a 25bps hike.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A sharper reacceleration in subsequent data or deteriorating inflation expectations would bring a 50bps hike into consideration. Friday's PPI and the October core PCE estimate should clarify the likelihood.

theme_stances.key_argument: The print strengthens the case for a 25bps December hike, but a 50bps move is unlikely unless data reaccelerate or inflation expectations deteriorate.
theme_stances.evidence: strengthens the case for a 25-basis point hike at the December meeting

theme_stances.key_argument: Elevated and accelerating supercore inflation signals that demand growth is outstripping supply.
